I am 64 years old. I never went to school, but I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My wife and I do all the work ourselves. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as every household in our village.

For wheat, I plough the field deep in October before sowing. I use the same improved wheat seed I have been saving for years — it works, so why change? Per mu, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer as base, that is 25 kg. When the wheat turns green in March, I topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. At heading I add another 5 kg if the leaves look yellow. All together that is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings settle in, once at jointing when they shoot up fast, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — herbicide right after sowing, and insecticide in spring if I see aphids or rust. Last year I got 500 kg per mu, and I will aim for the same.

For maize, right after we cut the wheat in June I rotary till quick and plant. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town, 2 to 3 jin per mu. I put down 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and when the plants are knee-high I spread another 15 kg of urea per mu. That is about 16 kg of nitrogen total. I irrigate twice — once after planting if the weather is hot and dry, and once when the tassels come out. One spray for corn borer is usually enough. I expect 550 kg per mu.

I watch old Zhang across the road. If he puts down a certain amount, I do the same. I would rather use a bit too much fertilizer than too little — a thin harvest is a disaster, but wasting half a bag of urea is just money spent. I count every yuan, but I sleep better knowing I fed my crops well.
